title: PLCG2 downregulation impairs synaptic function and increases Alzheimer's disease hallmarks in neuronal cultures.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Queried the ENA (European Nucleotide Archive) file report for PRJEB112198: 34 runs, all raw FASTQ (snRNA-seq, single-nucleus RNA sequencing, of shNT / shPLCG2 / PLCG2-WT / PLCG2-R953X human neuronal cultures, about 4 replicates each, roughly 5-45 GB per file; plus 2 whole-genome sequencing runs of 40-48 GB per file). ENA analysis report is empty, so no processed count matrix is deposited there. Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint timed out (75 s), so Supplementary Table 1 (the screen results) was not opened.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The high-content screen covers 198 AD (Alzheimer's disease) risk genes knocked down by shRNA (short hairpin RNA) in rat neurons, run three times, with results in Supplementary Table 1; per-figure source data and western blots; the case-control variant analyses (e.g. ADES cohort, 8,732 cases / 8,955 controls) are summary results only, individual-level data not shared.

a1_downloadable.note: ENA raw reads are open (checked file report); supplementary tables exist per paper but the supplement endpoint timed out, so not verified.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Screen table reportedly has normalized synaptic density per shRNA (paper text only); for snRNA-seq the only 'label' is the experimental condition, which is the design, not an outcome.

a3_inputs_present.note: snRNA-seq is raw FASTQ only (checked ENA, no processed analyses); a gene-level screen would need features built from external resources for each of 198 genes.

a4_units_stated.note: Synaptic density normalized to non-transduced wells per plate (paper methods); not checked in files.

a5_enough_rows.note: The screen is 198 genes (paper text), far under ~400 even for classification; snRNA-seq has about 16 samples across 4 conditions (checked ENA sample titles).

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~600+ GB of raw FASTQ (sum of per-file sizes seen in ENA)
a6_fits_laptop.note: No processed matrix deposited; would require alignment of hundreds of GB of reads, which is not a laptop job.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: ENA run titles match the 4-condition, 4-replicate design described; screen counts not checked.

a8_label_provenance.note: Synaptic density is a measured imaging readout, not a model output (paper text).

backbone.name: Geneformer or scGPT (single-cell foundation models) would apply to snRNA-seq, but only after raw read processing
backbone.hardware: Not reached; raw FASTQ processing needs a server
backbone.licence: Paper CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; ENA data open

integration.partner_dataset: SEA-AD (Seattle Alzheimer's Disease Brain Cell Atlas) snRNA-seq, which the paper itself uses
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Whether the PLCG2-knockdown signature in cultured neurons tracks dementia status in human brain neurons; the paper already does this as a statistical comparison, not an ML task.

controls.positive_control: shSyp (synaptophysin knockdown) wells in the screen
controls.external_validation: None for an ML task at this size

honest_claim_h3: With 198 screened genes, a model could at most claim to rank which AD-risk-locus genes lower synaptic density in rat neuron cultures, with far too few examples to validate.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use gene-level features of Alzheimer's risk genes to predict whether knocking each gene down reduces synapse numbers in cultured neurons.
plain_idea.train_on: One row per screened gene with features such as brain expression and protein embeddings; 198 genes (paper text, table not opened).
plain_idea.predict: Normalized synaptic density after shRNA knockdown, measured by automated imaging of pre- and postsynaptic markers in rat hippocampal neurons.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Would help prioritize which genes at Alzheimer's risk loci to test for synaptic effects, but 198 examples cannot support a trained model.

ml_idea: Predict per-gene synaptic-density effect from the 198-gene knockdown screen; rejected because n is far too small and the single-nucleus data are raw reads only.

effort.compute_note: Working set summed roughly from ENA per-file FASTQ sizes; nothing timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count rows in Supplementary Table 1 (expected 198 genes); already below threshold from paper text.

verdict_reason: A5 and A6 fail: the screen covers only 198 genes, and the single-nucleus RNA data are about 16 samples deposited as roughly 600 GB of raw FASTQ with no processed matrix (checked ENA). This is a mechanistic single-gene study with no ML-scale table.
